prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1010; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Initial report received from the insured driver's policy line describing a left-turn collision at an intersection. The insured driver is named on the policy and the vehicle was insured at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant's representing attorney, who confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle and reports neck and back pain following the impact. Requested the medical authorization and the treatment list.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle and records the other vehicle's involvement. No independent witnesses are listed, and no one has come forward since.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair shop show damage mostly in line with the described impact. Some details in the photos confirm the account, while others remain unclear and will need an inspection.

Entry 5: Took the claimant's recorded statement through counsel. The account of how the collision occurred matched what was given in the initial call and in the attorney's first letter.

Entry 6: Received the first treatment records. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of the crash, and the early care followed a usual course.

Entry 7: Prior medical history shows a small strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully with no ongoing care. Nothing in the records suggests the current complaint is a continuation of that episode.

Entry 8: Checked the vehicle history and found no earlier damage on file for this vehicle. Nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 9: Reviewed the later treatment notes, which show the claimant's symptoms tapering off as they improved with care. The file is being prepared for evaluation of the bodily injury portion of the claim.
